newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares off records, stable in late trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares off records, stable in late trade.

text.p: German IBIS DAX index lost momentum in afternoon electronic dealings to trade shy of record highs, but dealers again expressed amazement at the market's resilience.
In late afternoon trade the IBIS DAX index stood at 3,270.42 points, up 25.40 points. At one point in afternoon trade the index came within two points of its lifetime high of 3,286.37 points.
"This market is crazy, but let the cash roll in and just enjoy the ride," said one trader. "Most traders have discounted a correction already -- indeed they are hoping for it."
The dollar was one of the main factors behind the strength of the market. While slightly weaker against the mark at 1.68, it was still strong enough to underpin German share trade.
Among the main winners in afternoon trade was haircare marks after technical signals and dollar strength helped to boost the stock.

Also in favour was steel group Thyssen AG, up over five percent at 3,654.20 marks. Dealers said everyone was "jumping on the bandwagon", as market players sought to look for stocks which had been neglected in the bull run.
Sectoral rotation favoured builders Philipp Holzmann AG and Hochtief AG. Holzmann was up 4.24 percent at 492 marks, while Hochtief rose 1.50 marks to 73.20 marks later on.
Karstadt AG continued to enjoy favour over the day after reports of management changes. Shares ended the day up 3.17 percent at 554 marks.
Bayer AG also ended the day higher, up 1.56 marks at 71.28 marks, boosted by news that it planned to increase its research and development spending.
